steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Lou sai, all our sashimi comes freshly sliced. You don't get fresher fins than that. All our finballs are hand-kneaded, too. You don't get chewier balls than that. Line up in the back there.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Lou...

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Waai Fu?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: I'm delivering something for Uncle Lee. Just passing by.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: You've had your stall here the last couple days? No wonder I haven't seen you.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Th-The docks get lots of traffic. Finballs sell like hotcakes here.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: The only ones around at this hour are workers on their way home. You sure you can move more finballs here than the tourist spots?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Never mind. You're about to close up, right? Let's head back together. I'll wait for you.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Uh... I'm okay...

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Huh? What's wrong?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: N-Nothing. Well... Waai Fu, I... I've got something for you.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I, well, it's a graduation present...

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: A graduation present? Now?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Stop by my place when you have time. There's a spare key under the doormat.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: There's a big box in the bedroom. It's all in there, along with a couple things I wanted to tell you...

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I've had it prepared for a while, but after you graduated, you went to Shangshu and Yumen. I haven't had a lot of chances to give them to you, since you were hardly ever in Lungmen.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Don't forget to stop by.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: I should probably say thank you... but this is really weird. Who makes a girl fetch her own present?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Yeah, well... Say, isn't it your birthday on Saturday? Let me take you to the movies, and I'll bring the graduation present along with the one for your birthday.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You go home and get some rest now. I'll meet you at the mall tomorrow morning.
Ahem, lou sai.
You selling your finballs or not?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Oh, deoi m zyu.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: An order of finballs, double spice, yeah? Coming right up.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Your finballs.
That's the friend you said knows her kung fu, right? Surname Waai?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Yeah.
And she just graduated?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Yeah.
I'm thinking I could let her join the gang. A talented girl with solid moves. You don't get help like that easy.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Don't be stupid, Ah Wei.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I don't want her getting mixed up in this.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Alright... You're still worried.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: You don't trust me, huh? I told you already. We've got everyone here from the highest echelon to the bottom rung in our pockets. As long as these goods make it through the docks safe tonight, they'll disappear into the slums tomorrow morning. Nothing will happen.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Say you toss some limestone into the river ahead of us. When it's all dark out, who'll notice the bubbles on the surface?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I'm just a little nervous.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Yeah, I get it. It's your first time. You'll get used to it.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I told you. There is no next time.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Fine, fine. How's prep work going for your first and last time, then?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: The driver, inspector, and court clerk are all old friends, and I've already talked to them.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Tonight, all the cargo ships entering port will, coincidentally, have to go through a monthly inventory check and sorting, and because of the huge amount of cargo, from 10:00 to 10:30, the port will temporarily halt inspections of incoming cargo ships.

spans.text: Tonight, all the cargo ships entering port will,
have to go through a monthly inventory check and sorting, and because of the huge amount of cargo, from 10:00 to 10:30, the port will temporarily halt inspections of incoming cargo ships.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Have your ship come in at 10:15. You have fifteen minutes to unload your goods.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Have those ships greet us.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You don't trust me?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: This has nothing to do with that, Jaye. Show me.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: How do you want them do it?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Have the ship furthest to the left in the docks blink twice.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Uncle Fung, turn the searchlight on and off twice.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Let me hear the rightmost ship's whistle. Let's see if it's loud enough.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Big Cheung, blow the whistle twice for me, please.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: And have the ship in the middle head out for a quick spin?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Siu Kai, sorry. Help me out here.
I heard you guys... Heading out this late at night... You know that favor I owe you? We'll call it even with this.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Jaye, you may just be a seafood hawker, but you're the most reliable, promising seafood hawker in all of Lungmen!

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Remember what I told you when we were kids? When the two of us work together, anything's possible.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Even a simple drink has uses beyond imagination.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: They're all good guys. They have no idea what they're getting mixed up in.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I mean, remember what the adults in the neighborhood used to say when we were kids? 'There's no good or bad. There's only relationship.' Lungmen is a place where we talk relationship.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: That's a whole 'nother thing.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Anyway, I made the right call coming to you.
Twenty days earlier...

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Phew—
Lou sai, can I trade this for an order of finballs?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Sorry, I'm closed for the day—
The man sets an empty can down on the cutting board in front of Jaye.
The entire bottom side of the can is cut off, and the can is cut twice along an axis and bent outward into a curve, revealing its dark, silver interior.
It looks like a crude flower or something.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ah Wei?!

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Hey, Jaye. Been a while.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: It really is you! When did you get back? How did you find me? It's been at least a decade since the last time we saw each other, right? Where did you go after you left Lungmen?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I came looking for you right after I made my way back here. As for how I found you...

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Don't forget you took on two whole gangs all by yourself. Everybody in Lungmen knows you. They call you 'stone-faced finball bossman,' 'ice-cold Jaye,' and stuff.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: That was just an accident... Stop making fun of me.
The man picks up the carved can, on which the light of the street is faintly reflected.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I didn't think you'd still remember.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Of course I do.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: When we were in third grade, you brought a bunch of empty cans home with you, and your mom scolded you for bringing back trash. But then you used them to make little trinkets like this, fixed the antenna, and got the broken TV working again.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Metal strengthens signals, and I was just tinkering.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ever since, you scoured the alleyways and collected empty cans. One day, you would make an incense holder. The next day, a communications terminal. You saved your family lots of money.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I even took you in as my goon. You followed me everywhere.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Yeah, our houses were right next to each other. The neighbors liked to compare us, but they always complimented you, said you'd do great things when you grew up. I was jealous.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Not like me... I'm not nearly as bright, so all I could do was learn how to make finballs from Uncle Tung.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: So, are you just visiting, or are you staying for good this time?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Nah, I'm staying.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Great! I've been helping clean your place. It's in pretty good shape. Just move some furniture, toiletries, and stuff in and you can start...

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Yeah, Jaye, I need your help.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I brought a shipment of goods back to Lungmen to sell.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Nice! So you're in business now. Lungmen's pretty strict with inspections, but I can help you run them by the L.G.D.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: My goods aren't on the L.G.D.'s list of approved imports and exports.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Y-You're smuggling?!

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Weapons? Originium products? Illegal drugs? What's with the hands. Is that some kind of signal? I-I don't know what you're getting at.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Nobody knows about this. We've been planning it for a while. It's all under wraps, I guarantee.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Besides, the risk and return are proportional. Jaye, I know you know the guys at the docks.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I've been away from Lungmen for over a decade. I don't know the place anymore. I need money, and I need to do this deal to get back on my feet. You're the only one who can help.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: No, I'm not doing it. You shouldn't, either.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Oh yeah. Why did you come around in the end again?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: It's ten after ten... The ship is about to come in.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Where are the guys picking up the merch? Have them stand by at the port. We've only got fifteen minutes.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Don't worry. Just a little longer.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Officer Hoshiguma, it's almost time. Why is it still quiet?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Maybe we got a bad tip?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Relax. We can trust this informant.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Hallucinatory drugs made from purified Originium... No one in the Lungmen black markets would dare deal in something like this. Why is someone smuggling something this hot all of a sudden?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: The Rat King hasn't been taking his usual walks, has he?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: I heard he was hurt bad on his trip to Yumen. Do you mean...?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Lin Yühsia isn't going to Victoria anymore. But I doubt her plan to become the 'Lin the Violet' is gonna go all that smooth.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Looks like there are some fussy folks who want to find out for the old man whether his daughter is worthy of his chair.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: The gangs in the slums, big and small, have been making lots of noise, and the L.G.D. has been busy with all that.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: But I guess these folks have forgotten the L.G.D.'s hard stance against contraband.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: 10:16. Fourteen minutes left.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: The ship's docked. On the double, everyone. Watch your surroundings, and keep two men on watch.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I didn't expect you to have so many guys on this job.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Why not? This is a huge deal. Lots of hands want a slice of the pie.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Jaye, you look nervous.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: You keep watch here. I'll go check things out.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: *sigh*... Ah Wei, the ship's that way. Why are you heading for the exit?

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Officer Hoshiguma, should we move in?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Hold on. These are no normal gangsters. They're on high alert. Wait until they fall into our trap. We'll catch both the men and the goods together.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: We're not letting any of these drugs into Lungmen. And we're not letting a single perp escape.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Remember to keep the informant safe.

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Officer! Looks like the boss is trying to run!

steps.name: L.G.D. Officer
steps.text: Not a chance!

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Wait! He's definitely just testing...

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ah Wei! Don't run! You can't!

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: All units, move in!
Jaye keeps running.
He most likely bumped into a few passersby, and he definitely knocked over the fruit stand on the street corner. He keeps muttering, 'deoi m zyu,' but he doesn't stop.
His friend is right ahead. His friend is still running.

He has no time to even think about which streets he has been running through. He notices nothing except how there are less and less people, the roads are getting narrower, and his surroundings are getting quieter. So quiet, he can hear nothing but his and his friend's panting.
The oxygen deprivation is causing him to hallucinate.
Jaye starts to think he is running down that alley he used to run down as a kid—
He is following his 'Soda Can Magician' friend, through the shades of the banyan trees and out the slums, as they both planned to go together, towards a brighter future.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: S-Stop running. My lungs are about to blow.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: There's nowhere to go up ahead... It's a dead end.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ah Wei.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: You sold me out.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I got a good thing going on, and you're the first one I went to with it.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I know you're a coward for how mean you look. You're a good guy, and all you wanna do is sell fins and finballs. I get that. You turning down the offer? I was fine with that. That's no skin off my back.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I did have my suspicions when you came back to me a week later and said you were in. But you're Jaye. I knew Jaye would follow me, just like he used to when we were kids.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: We never kept anything from each other. You even taught me the knife skills you learned from Uncle Tung. I never lied to you, and you never lied to me.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: But this time, you were lying to me right from the start.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ah Wei, l-listen...

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Who are you snitching for? Another gang? The L.G.D.?
Two weeks ago...

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: How's business been?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Officer Hoshiguma?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Do you need something from me?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Well, I'm sure you wouldn't believe me if I told you I was just passing by and decided to get a couple of orders of finballs for my lads back at the station.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: That would've been nice, wouldn't it?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I thought I'd stop by to give you a heads up. The Char Sius and Lou Seois' bosses are about to be released.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: They're scum, but they're still gangsters. You threw a wrench in their plans, and they lost face among the Lungmen triads, thanks to you. They just might make trouble for you.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Oh—

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: No need to be scared. The L.G.D. can offer you protection, if you want.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Yeah, thanks, Officer. Here's an order of finballs. It's on me. Have a nice day.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I'm not done yet. Are you merchants always so afraid to deal with the L.G.D.?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I want to ask you about something.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Have you been to the ports lately?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I went just this morning to settle my bill for the month.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Have you seen anyone or anything suspicious?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Suspicious, huh...?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Anyone who's been asking about the ships, policies on the flow of goods, inspection procedures, that sort of thing.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Officer, is something going on? That port is the biggest seafood market in Lungmen. If something happens and the stalls at the market get shut down, everyone's gonna be out of a job...

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Relax. I'm just hypothesizing here.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: According to our sources, someone is about to smuggle a shipment of illegal drugs into the slums.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: The L.G.D. caught wind of it a little too late, and the shipment might already have made it into Lungmen. We're investigating all logistics channels right now... The gateway, city beltway, the port.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: (And he said it's all under wraps...)

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Oh, nothing.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Anyway, you know the port better than I do, so I want you to pay attention to the people there and see if there's any movement. If you notice anything, give me a call.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Yeah, I will.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: This's pretty serious, right, Officer?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Is this smuggling case serious?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: The detectives have this shipment listed as highly dangerous illegal contraband. It's on a whole other level from the Originium Devices that the Char Sius removed from those weapons to sell.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: If you find anything... you have my number.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Well, off I go then. Thanks for the finballs.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Hold on, Officer Hoshiguma.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: So you snitched on me to the L.G.D. and started spying for them?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I did it because...

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: It's all gone. I put a whole decade of savings into this deal! And now it's all gone!

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Well, I guess it's for the best.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Who ever said Jaye's a coward, a small man, an ordinary guy? You're way more of a badass than the undercover cops in the triad shows. They're all acting, but you're the real deal, as brave as it gets.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Calm down. Hear me out.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: I don't want to hear another word from you. Later. We'll pretend I never came back.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ah Wei, I can't let you go just like that.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: What more do you want? The successful sting's not good enough for you? You want to take the perp in yourself, too?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: What, are they going to name you citizen of the month?

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Go look over there.

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Search through every one of these alleyways. Don't let anyone get away.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Jaye, move.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Your plan's a bust. Your buyers won't let you off easy. You're in with some merciless guys.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: That's why I'm leaving Lungmen right now.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I'm not letting you go.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Hmph... Don't say I didn't warn—Hm?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I swiped your weapon back at the port.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You remember how we never held any grudges against each other for more than a day? Every time we had a difference of opinion, we worked through it the same way.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Like this!
Jaye punches his friend square in the face.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: So anyone involved in this smuggling operation will get a much harsher sentence than the Char Sius and the Lou Seois?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Like... how harsh are we talking?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: All the guys wanted to do last time was sell crude, shoddy Originium products. Besides, you busted them halfway through, and they also owned up to the whole thing with a pretty good attitude throughout, so they got light sentences.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: That said, the bosses still got two years in the can.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: But if our intel's correct, they're smuggling some powerful hallucinogens. On paper, they're just very hard to get 'painkillers' and 'sedatives' that work fast.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: But, of course, they don't come with any instructions, and they don't tell the users about any potential side effects—that the trace amounts of purified Originium can accelerate the deterioration of Oripathy.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Th-That's dirty money.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: It's gonna make the patients severely dependent.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: The Lungmenites tormented by sickness will have both their last pennies and last breaths of life sucked dry. They'll bring a herd infection that's even more uncontrollable.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: That's why the L.G.D. has always enforced hard on this kind of contraband, and even the triads rarely deal in this stuff.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: The mastermind will have to spend the rest of his life behind bars.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: That's a serious crime...

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Then what if it's only attempted? Would that make any difference? What if they turn themselves in? Does that make the sentence any lighter?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Where did you learn all that...?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: T-Tell me, Officer.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: If it hasn't caused any severe, irreparable harm yet, then there's still room to turn things around.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: But even if they manage to escape, if they have a criminal record, they'll never be allowed to in Lungmen again.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Can't come back to Lungmen, huh?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Alright, Jaye, I've answered all your questions.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Now it's your turn to tell me what you know.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Officer Hoshiguma, I want you to help a friend of mine.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: You don't have to help me, but you didn't have to backstab me like that!

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ah Wei, I am helping you!
A series of muffled, rhythmic sounds can be heard. Deep in the back alley, the two men exchange blows.
Like some kind of silly, turn-based game.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You used to make antennas, incense holders, and comms terminals out of soda cans.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You were the 'Soda Can Magician,' you were my hero, you were so smart. Just an amazing guy.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You should never have gone down this path!

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Do you know why I had to leave Lungmen all those years ago? You probably heard that my family ran into some kind of trouble, but you have no idea what exactly happened, right?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: It was a stupid gang fight. Two sides had a turf war and got into it, and the bosses had to send in guys to clean things up.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: My parents just happened to pass by. We had nothing to do with the triads. Why would we?

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Do you know who was in charge of the cleanup? Why do you think I left Lungmen without so much as coming to say good bye?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: ...Uncle Tung.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: 'Soda Can Magician?' Magician my ass!

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: In Lungmen, soda cans get kicked around and dumped in trash cans.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: But I don't blame you. You're Jaye. This has nothing to do with you. It doesn't even have anything to do with Uncle Tung. Because this is Lungmen. 'There's no good or bad. All that matters is survival.'

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: You know, even if you didn't join me on this gig, once I had the money, I was going to help you franchise your finball stall.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: We were going to take those finballs all over the country. Shangshu, Jiangqi, Yumen. Even beyond Yan.
Jaye takes a few punches and slowly backs up against the wall. He steps on something, slips, and falls to the ground.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I don't need that.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Living on dirty money... I can't have that on my conscience.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Ah Wei, you know that people could die because of those drugs you were smuggling, right?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I don't know what you've been through over the last ten years. I'm sure you've done all sorts of things to survive. Everybody's got a different way to get by, right?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You don't have to have lots of money. You don't have to be in a position of power.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Has Lungmen really changed? The slums, the port, the park, the seafood market... There are so many folks here, trying their hardest, living life without hurting anybody.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: You're such an amazing guy. What's stopping you from doing that?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I can help you.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I'm tired. I-I've got nothing left to say.
Jaye lies down on the ground. A stream of blood gushes out of his forehead and wells up in the corner of his eye.
He shuts his eye hard to keep the blood from flowing into his eye. He has always looked like a pretty mean guy, and with how his face is bloodied, he now looks all the more ferocious.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: *sigh*—

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Goodbye.
The man isn't able to step away. He looks down to find his brother, his eye barely open, clinging to his leg.
Just like when they were both kids, he is a quiet guy, but he is as stubborn as one can be.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: Jaye, let go. I really don't want to hurt you.
Jaye does not answer, nor does he let go.
The man grits his teeth, leans down, and pulls the scaling knife out of Jaye's pocket.

steps.name: Ah Wei
steps.text: This is your fault.

All of a sudden, the man finds that he has come face-to-face with Jaye, both of them on the muddy ground. Yet he feels not the slightest bit of cold, perhaps because of the numbness from the intense impact.
The very moment before his consciousness drifts away, he faintly spots a terribly dented soda can. Perhaps that was the thing that crashed into his head mere seconds ago.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Phew—

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Made it just in time.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: That's about the size of it.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: All the merchandise have been recovered. The overseas smugglers and the local recipients have all been taken in by the L.G.D.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Thanks, Madame Oni.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: How are things on your end?

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: We may have put a stop to the problem upstream, but those downstream aren't blameless. I put together a list of the ones in the slums waiting to distribute. And I paid each of them a visit before I came here.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: I won't trouble the L.G.D. with our housework.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Should've expected no less from the 'Lin the Violet,' huh?

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: It's nothing. My dad's still resting up after his injuries, and I don't want him to get out of bed.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Right, he wanted to ask. How was Jaye on this sting?

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: He was hurt, but it was nothing serious.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Without him, we wouldn't have been able to wrap up this operation at the port or round them up so easily.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: If even an ounce of this shipment had made it into Lungmen, things would've got much trickier.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Even outside the slums, there are plenty of gangs who would be willing to deal in hallucinatory drugs of this level. Taking care of it all right up front is the safest approach, of course.

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: But Jaye's just a normal guy, and given Uncle Tung's age, Dad doesn't want him to...

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: I get it. The situation's unique... but rest assured the L.G.D. will protect its informants.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: And how is Mr. Lin's prognosis?

steps.name: Lin Yühsia
steps.text: Fair. He still wants to sneak outside to play weiqi with his old friends.

steps.name: Hoshiguma
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Oh, you're finally awake.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Oww... that's a sharp pain.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Of course it hurts when you do that to your face.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Don't move. I'm putting on some ointment.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: How's Ah Wei?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: The L.G.D. guys took him away.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Speaking of which, Officer Hoshiguma wants you to head to the station for a written statement after you rest up.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: So, why were you playing hero behind my back again?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: You went undercover, and on a case where the smugglers are all actual bad guys, not like those Char Siu thugs last time! One of the L.G.D. guys got hurt while they were taking the smugglers in.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Why didn't you ask for my help? You almost lost your life back there, you know?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: (That's why I didn't want to drag you into this...)

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: What are you mumbling about?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Nothing... Say, I thought you were running errands for Mr. Lee? What are you doing back here?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: You were talking funny. I knew something was up.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: And I haven't even asked you yet. You said you had a graduation present for me, and you wrote something down... What is it supposed to mean?

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: Well, I did actually get you a graduation present...

steps.name: Jaye
steps.text: How was that talking funny...?

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: Not the graduation present. My birthday.

steps.name: Waai Fu
steps.text: It's Sunday, not Saturday. How'd you get that wrong?
